source.title: Gemma Scope: Open Sparse Autoencoders Everywhere All At Once on Gemma 2
source.authors: Tom Lieberum; Senthooran Rajamanoharan; Arthur Conmy; Lewis Smith; Nicolas Sonnerat; Vikrant Varma; J'anos Kram'ar; Anca D. Dragan; Rohin Shah; Neel Nanda

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; minor PDF extraction and figure-layout artifacts do not prevent reading.
record.tranche_reason: Applies sparse autoencoders to Gemma 2 models and reports reconstruction and sparsity results, extending SAE-based feature recovery to these models. It does not test the toy-model superposition geometry itself.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates SAE reconstruction and latent statistics on Gemma 2. These results bear on SAE recovery in LLMs (V4), but do not directly measure underlying feature geometry or whether SAE latents are complete, canonical model units. Interpretability-rating and explanation results are reproduced from Rajamanoharan et al. (2024b), so they are not recorded as this study’s own results. Figure-only values are not inferred.
record.test_reason: Gemma Scope is a resource paper. It trains JumpReLU SAEs on Gemma 2 and reports only its own method's performance: sparsity–fidelity curves, width ladders, firing frequencies, transfer to IT models, Pile subsets and precision. It assumes activations are sparse linear combinations of features and uses SAEs as the tool. It does not test whether real model features are superposed, distributed across neurons, or recovered by the SAE. The authors list whether SAEs find 'true' concepts as an open problem. Reconstruction quality of the authors' own SAEs is method performance, not a test of V4. No version receives a verdict.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. More precisely, the paper releases an open suite of JumpReLU SAEs on Gemma 2 2B/9B (and selected 27B layers) with standard evaluations. These include sparsity–fidelity, position, width, base-to-IT transfer, Pile subsets and bf16 inference. The authors stress that there is no consensus SAE-quality metric and that whether SAEs find true concepts is open.
record.recipe_differences: Trains JumpReLU SAEs on Gemma 2 model activations and evaluates sparsity–reconstruction trade-offs; it does not reproduce the original toy-network superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Reconstruction fidelity varies with SAE width and sparsity; the paper also reports different delta-loss behavior across SAE sites and a shift in latent firing frequencies with width.

fits_no_version.finding: Wider SAEs give better delta-loss versus L0 at matched sparsity coefficient. Latent firing frequencies shift lower with width, but an ultra-high-frequency cluster persists.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE width changes reconstruction fidelity and the latent frequency distribution.

fits_no_version.finding: Attribution-weighted importance becomes more diffuse as L0 rises, most strongly for residual-stream SAEs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The importance distribution over active SAE latents depends on L0 and site.

fits_no_version.finding: SAEs trained on base Gemma 2 9B reconstruct IT-model rollout activations with delta loss nearly as small as IT-trained SAEs. The FVU gap is larger.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAEs trained on base-model activations transfer to instruction-tuned derivatives.

fits_no_version.finding: Delta loss is consistently higher for residual-stream SAEs than for MLP or attention SAEs, while FVU is roughly comparable across sites. SAEs do best on DM mathematics and worst on Europarl.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE reconstruction cost varies by site and data domain.

record.peer_reviewed: BlackboxNLP Workshop on Analyzing and Interpreting Neural Networks for NLP
record.problems: The paper notes there is no consensus on reliable SAE-quality metrics. Reconstruction fidelity does not by itself establish that recovered latents are true or complete model features. Several plotted results do not have numerical values stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No other relevant numeric or text-described results were omitted. Values available only as plots were not transcribed.

untested.parts: No toy models, geometry or sparsity transition.
No alternative causes of polysemanticity are examined.

Does not measure feature distribution across neurons. Does not validate that SAE latents correspond to the model's features; this is posed as an open problem. SAE reconstruction is reported only as tool performance.
Completeness, stability and canonicity are not tested. Feature splitting and missed features are cited from other work as open problems.
Not tested. Circular and multi-dimensional features (Engels et al.) are only cited as an open problem.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T3' and its V4 'supports' label are overturned. The paper uses SAEs as a tool and reports their engineering performance. The interpretability results (Figs. 6–7) are reproduced from Rajamanoharan et al. 2024b and were correctly excluded. Superposition is mentioned only in the introduction and the open-problems list.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test toy networks, feature overlap or orthogonality, interference, or a sparsity-dependent geometric transition.
Does not test whether neurons become polysemantic because features compete for model capacity, or whether important features receive dedicated model dimensions.
Does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons.

Tests SAE reconstruction on Gemma 2 activations, but not whether features are distributed across neurons, whether recovered latents correspond to the model’s true semantic features, or whether this holds beyond the evaluated Gemma 2 settings.
Does not establish SAE features as complete, stable, or canonical units; these are raised as open questions.
SAE decoder columns are directions, but the paper does not test whether the underlying model features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: Gemma 2 2B PT
rows.operation_detail: Compared reconstruction fidelity across a ladder of residual-stream SAE widths at matched sparsity settings.

conditions.value: matched sparsity coefficients; curves sweep sparsity

rows.measure: SAE reconstruction fidelity at a given sparsity
rows.baseline: narrower-width SAEs at the same sparsity
rows.value: Wide SAEs provide better reconstruction fidelity at a given level of sparsity than narrow SAEs; plotted values are figure only.
rows.note: The paper states the width comparison in text; the plotted numerical values are not stated.
rows.check: This is SAE method performance (reconstruction versus width), not a measure of superposition in the model. Figure 4 shows only Gemma 2 9B layer 20, so no plotted 2B width-ladder result supports this row. The width statement is framed as a general 'holding all else equal' intuition rather than a reported 2B result.

rows.subject: Gemma 2 9B PT
rows.operation_detail: Compared reconstruction fidelity across a ladder of residual-stream SAE widths at matched sparsity settings.

conditions.value: matched sparsity coefficients; curves sweep sparsity

rows.measure: SAE reconstruction fidelity at a given sparsity
rows.baseline: narrower-width SAEs at the same sparsity
rows.value: Wide SAEs provide better reconstruction fidelity at a given level of sparsity than narrow SAEs; plotted values are figure only.
rows.note: The paper states the width comparison in text; the plotted numerical values are not stated.
rows.check: This shows the study's own SAE performance across widths (Figure 4, 9B layer 20). It bears on SAE behaviour, not on whether the LLM contains superposed features. Delink from V4.

rows.subject: Gemma 2 9B PT
rows.operation_detail: Measured SAE latent firing-frequency distributions at different SAE widths.
rows.value: With increased latent count, the mode and most of the mass shift toward lower firing frequencies; a cluster of ultra-high-frequency latents remains.
rows.note: This describes how SAE latents are allocated across firing frequencies, not model-neuron polysemanticity or superposition geometry.
rows.check: This is an SAE latent statistic, not the claim. The link to none is correct.

rows.subject: Gemma 2 2B PT and Gemma 2 9B PT
rows.operation_detail: Measured the uniformity of attribution-weighted active SAE latents as sparsity varied.
rows.value: The attributed effect becomes more diffuse as more latents are active; the effect is most pronounced for residual-stream SAEs and appears independent of model size and SAE latent count.
rows.note: The paper reports this as a property of attribution-weighted SAE latents, not as a test of the claim’s feature geometry.
rows.check: This is an SAE attribution-uniformity metric (Appendix C.3, Fig. 16), not the claim. The link to none is correct.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Gemma 2 2B PT and Gemma 2 9B PT, middle-layer post-MLP residual-stream SAEs
reader_labels.reason: Wider SAE dictionaries achieve better reconstruction fidelity at the same sparsity, consistent with SAE recovery of model activations in these tested settings (r1, r2). This does not establish semantic or canonical feature recovery.
